did_you_know.text: Did you know? Hezekiah responded to the Assyrian threat by tearing his clothes, putting on sackcloth, and entering the house of the LORD; his actions expressed mourning, distress, and turning to the LORD.
Did you know? Hezekiah sent Eliakim, Shebna, and the elders of the priests to Isaiah, and all of them were wearing sackcloth.

Did you know? Hezekiah’s messengers described the situation as “a day of distress, rebuke, and disgrace” and compared it to a woman who has reached the time of childbirth but has no strength to give birth.
Did you know? Isaiah declared in the name of the LORD that Sennacherib would hear a report, return to his own land, and fall by the sword there.
Did you know? After hearing that Tirhakah, king of Cush, had set out to fight him, Sennacherib again sent messengers to Hezekiah to intimidate him.

Did you know? Hezekiah took the letters from Sennacherib, read them, went up to the house of the LORD, and spread them out before the LORD; in this way, he turned the military threat into a matter of prayer.
Did you know? In his prayer, Hezekiah calls the LORD “the One enthroned above the cherubim” and emphasizes that he alone is God over all the kingdoms of the earth, the Creator of heaven and earth.
Did you know? Hezekiah asks for deliverance not only for Jerusalem’s sake, but also so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that the LORD alone is God.

Did you know? The sign given to Hezekiah describes the land’s gradual recovery: in the first year they would eat what grows on its own, in the second year what springs up from that, and in the third year they would sow, reap, and eat the fruit of the vineyards.
Did you know? According to the account, the angel of the LORD struck 185,000 men in the Assyrian camp; when morning came, they were all dead bodies.
